topic: The Windmill Problem (Computational Geometry & Rotational Invariants)
target_audience: Advanced high school students or undergraduate math students

sections.title: Problem Introduction: The Spinning Line
lecture_lines: Start with n points on a 2D plane.
A line passes through one point, acting as pivot.
The line rotates, sweeping like a radar.
It hits another point and pivots again.
We want to prove it hits every point.
animations: 1. Display a scattered set of 5 points #FFFFFF.
2. Draw a line #FFFF00 through one point as a pivot.
3. Rotate the line #FF0000 to strike another point.
4. Change pivot to the new point #00FF00.
5. Flash the entire path #FFFFFF to indicate connectivity.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Angles and Slopes
lecture_lines: Total angle rotated is the key invariant.
Each pivot switch adds a positive angle.
animations: 1. Draw an angle arc #FFFF00 between two intersecting lines.
3. Display slope formula #FF00FF and highlight change in value.

sections.title: The Core Mechanism: The Pivot Rule
lecture_lines: Geometry defines how the line pivots.
The line snaps to the next available point.
Think of it like a shifting bicycle gear.
This continues for every point encounter.
Geometry ensures a smooth, continuous transition.
animations: 1. Render a center point as pivot #00FF00.
2. Draw a line segment #FFFF00 radiating from the pivot.
3. Rotate line #FFFF00 until it hits a new point.
4. Update pivot to the new point #FF0000.
5. Show dashed path #FFFFFF indicating the sweep.

sections.title: The Invariant Principle
lecture_lines: Conservation of rotation drives the proof.
Total angle is finite in one sweep.
The line must visit every point eventually.
animations: 1. Display a total rotation angle indicator #FFFFFF.
2. Animate cumulative sum growth #FFFF00 as the line sweeps.
3. Flash the invariant total angle #00FF00 to confirm.

sections.title: Synthesis & Summary
lecture_lines: The Windmill uses invariants for dynamics.
Continuous angular accumulation proves the goal.
